# Split runner.py along a call-graph seam — it sits at exactly the 800-LOC hard cap

## Problem

`src/rebar/llm/runner.py` is **exactly 800 LOC** (`wc -l`), which is the repo hard cap in
`.github/module-size-limit.txt`. The CI module-size gate compares with `$1 > lim` (strictly greater), so 800
PASSES today — but there is **zero headroom**: the next line added to this file fails `Verified` for everyone.

This is a pre-existing condition, not caused by one story: runner.py was 783 before `7468`, 787 before `dc0d`.
`AGENTS.md` targets **200–500 LOC** per file, so it is well past target.

It is now a **hard blocker, not a nicety**. Both remaining code stories in epic `061c` must ADD lines to this
file and cannot:

- `2932` (Bedrock) adds a `supports_temperature` capability check plus the cache-zero warning;
- `343b` (verdict provenance) adds provenance capture.

Both are strictly positive LOC, so there is no net-neutral way to write them. This task is recorded as `blocks`
on both.

## Approach — the seam, chosen from measured data

`AGENTS.md`: split only along call-graph seams that already exist, never mechanically to hit a number, and never
create a file under 100 LOC. Measured top-level symbol sizes in the current file:

| symbol | lines |
|---|---|
| `PydanticAIRunner` | 400 |
| `_pai_structured` | 76 |
| `RunRequest` | 47 |
| `FakeRunner` | 44 |
| `_extract_usage` | 34 |
| `_pai_check_config` | 29 |
| `_readonly_gate` | 21 |
| `get_runner` / `Runner` / `_check_tool_capability` | 19 / 17 / 17 |
| `_warn_if_zeroed_usage` | 16 |
| `_import_pydantic_ai` | 13 |
| `effective_max_tokens` / `effective_max_iterations` | 10 / 9 |
| `_FAULTY_OUTPUT_SNIPPET_CHARS` | 3 |

**Extract the structured-output execution cluster** into a new leaf `src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py`:

- `_pai_structured` (76) — the bounded structured-output retry driver
- `_extract_usage` (34) — which `_pai_structured` calls twice
- `_warn_if_zeroed_usage` (16) — which interprets what `_extract_usage` returns
- `effective_max_iterations` (9) + `effective_max_tokens` (10) — the per-request budget sizing the retry loop
  and `run()` both enforce
- `_FAULTY_OUTPUT_SNIPPET_CHARS` (3) — used only by `_pai_structured`

**= 148 lines moved.** `runner.py` lands at ~657 (under the 700 target below, with real headroom), and
`structured_run.py` is ~165–175 LOC with its docstring and imports — comfortably over the 100-LOC floor.

**Why this is a genuine seam and not a mechanical carve.** Verified by reading the cluster: `_pai_structured`
references exactly `_extract_usage`, `_FAULTY_OUTPUT_SNIPPET_CHARS`, and `RunRequest`; everything else it uses is
`rebar.llm.contracts` / `rebar.llm.structured` / `pydantic_ai`, all already deferred function-local imports. The
cluster is "drive a structured-output run and account its token usage" — the members call each other and nothing
else in the file calls into the middle of them.

**The one snag, and its resolution.** `_pai_structured`'s signature annotates `req: RunRequest`, and `RunRequest`
stays in `runner.py` (moving it would churn every `from rebar.llm.runner import RunRequest` site across the
tests for no benefit). With `from __future__ import annotations` the annotation is a string at runtime, so
`structured_run.py` imports `RunRequest` under `if TYPE_CHECKING:` only. There is therefore **no runtime import
from `runner`**, which is what the leaf rule actually protects against — matching the convention already used by
`anthropic_model.py`, `providers.py` and `capabilities.py`.

`runner.py` imports the five moved callables from `structured_run`. Direction is runner -> structured_run, never
back.

**Rejected alternatives.** (a) Moving `_pai_check_config` (29) to `config.py` — the obvious quick win, but
`config.py` is 768 LOC so it would land at ~796 and merely relocate the same landmine. (b) A tiny module holding
only `_extract_usage` + `_warn_if_zeroed_usage` (50 lines) — violates the sub-100-LOC split rule. (c) Splitting
`PydanticAIRunner.run()` itself (the real 400-line bulk) — a much larger behavioural risk, and not needed to
clear the cap; worth its own story if runner.py trends up again.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py` (**new leaf**) — the five moved symbols.
- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — the symbols removed and imported instead.
- Test import sites for the moved symbols. **Enumerate them with a symbol-reference query, not by eye**, and
  sweep separately for string-literal patch targets (`monkeypatch.setattr(runner_mod, "_pai_structured", ...)`)
  which an LSP cannot resolve — that exact class broke `7468` and `f184` in this epic. Known at time of writing:
  `tests/interfaces/store/test_execution_mode_dispatch.py` patches `runner_mod._pai_structured` by string.

## Testing

**This is a pure relocation with no behaviour change, so it cannot be RED-first, and pretending otherwise would
be dishonest.** The oracle is the existing suite: 7517 tests currently pass, and they must still pass with no
edits other than moved import sites and patch targets. A behaviour change here shows up as a failure in tests
written for the behaviour, which is exactly the regression net this split needs.

The only genuinely new assertion is the structural one: that `structured_run.py` has no runtime import from
`runner`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] no file under `src/rebar` exceeds **700** LOC — real headroom, not sitting on the cap. (`runner.py`
      projected ~657.)
- [ ] `src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py` is >= 100 LOC (the `AGENTS.md` floor for a split)
- [ ] `structured_run.py` has NO runtime import from `runner`: `grep -n 'from rebar.llm.runner\|import runner'
      src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py` shows only a `TYPE_CHECKING`-guarded line, if any
- [ ] `import rebar.llm` still pulls in NO heavy module (httpx / anthropic / pydantic_ai / openai / boto3),
      verified empirically — heavy imports stay function-local
- [ ] the FULL gating suite passes with **7517 passed** and zero test-logic edits: only import sites and
      string-literal patch targets may change, proving behaviour preservation
- [ ] every moved symbol's reference sites were found via a symbol-reference query PLUS a string-literal grep,
      and both were run (the string-literal sweep is what an LSP structurally cannot do)
- [ ] [operator-attested] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the FULL `make test` pass, evidenced by the Gerrit
      change id and its `Verified +1` recorded in a comment on this ticket (this proof is external to the repo)
